Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This is a good programmable movement game for 2 - 4 players. You draft a set of movement cards, then organize them into a plan of action for your turn, and you let your mole loose on the dirt. Everywhere you pass, you add to the pile of dirt until your dirt piles get so large that they topple over, which usually happens near the end of every game...

...but the real fun of this game is the rock. If your mole hits the rock, which moves around each round at the whim of the player who drafts the right card, then you bump, switch directions, and watch your plan fail and falter. It's funny, even for the person who gets messed up because of it.

So this is a very fun game that is light and easy to learn. I wish the underground was a little clearer in terms of where the spaces are, or that the moles were a little bit better sized for the pieces. It works though.
text_fidelity_b: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+

text_fidelity_a:
Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.
text_fidelity_b: Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea

NEHEME NH525 Foldable Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, RC Quadcopter WiFi FPV Live Video, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Take Off for Kids/Beginners with 2 Batteries and Carry Case I didn't expect this drone to be so tiny but no matter. It was a good introduction to drone flying for me. I had planned on attaching a camera and expanding on my photography using this.

I will definitely need a bigger drone before I can do that but at least I was able to learn how to fly a drone since this is the first time I have ever had an experience with flying one.

What I enjoy about this is that it is easy to fly and the instruction manual was fairly easy to understand. It is small and lightweight so won't really injure somebody if it happens to crash land on somebody.

The drone itself has an extra set of blades in case the blades that are already on it get broken, as well as extra batteries for the drone itself. It even comes with a screw driver so you can open the battery compartments. This way no hunting down your own tools.

The remote used to fly the drone however requires some AAA batteries, which did not come with it but you can get those just about anywhere. The control looks much like a video game controller so kids and teens who are already adept with holding a video game pad will be able to master this in no time.

The drone performed well on its intitial flight for me, and I even got it to do a few flips and rolls as well.

This is a decent little starter drone.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH525 Foldable Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, RC Quadcopter WiFi FPV Live Video, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Take Off for Kids/Beginners with 2 Batteries and Carry Case

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue We enjoyed using this kit. I did it mostly with my 7 and 10 year old children. My 7 year old was the most interested. My 5 year old had interest, but he wasn't as gentle with it as he needed to be.

I especially like that the projects are centered around a story. You read a little, then build, read, build..... It makes the whole thing more fun and puts things into perspective. Everything you need is provided in the box, except for 2 AA batteries(so have those on hand before starting). The projects can get a little complicated, particularly when the gears come into the story, but it's not too bad. Some children might need help(or it can simply be a challenge to see if they can figure it out on their own).

The quality is mostly nice. The treehouse is made out of sheets of wood, and it seems durable to me. It won't last through rough play, but for the project, it holds up well. When building the treehouse, you can glue the pieces into place. We chose to take it apart, so we could do the projects again later with my youngest child. (Untying the knots was a bit of a pain, but otherwise, it's pretty simple to take apart.) There are a few pieces that are paper, though, and these are much less durable.

If you're looking for a fun project for a rainy day of learning, this is a nice kit to try.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue

TEAM MAGNUS 18ft XL Slip and Slide - Heavy Duty Inflatable Slide with Central Sprinkler and XL Crash Pad I’ve used the slide on a slight slope and almost a flat surface. PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. CON’s: the streaming water that “wets” the slide is too wide near the end of the slide and hardly existing at the start of the slide. The splash zone edges (inflated) nearest to the slide don’t ensure participant won’t slide over and miss splash zone.
A simple design improvement would be to have far less watering holes for the slip and slide near the splash zone and progressively more as you near the starting point. This to be is the largest flaw in the slide.
There are ways to “work around” the lack of water on the slide (the lack of slipperiness) but the product should fix this vs the customer having workarounds.

After years of mostly disappointing results with another popular bulk bag, I decided to try Wiz Dice. My very first bag I ordered had 16 full sets! I am the type of person who likes to have matching sets for completion sake, especially as I often give these sets away to new players. That was where my disappointment in the other brand stems from.
Of course, I ordered more as my needs demanded, and have always gotten at least 10+ sets with a few incomplete ones that I would set aside. I did this because Wiz dice uses a very limited color pallet, and I knew I would be able to complete those sets as the dice rolled in. Great colors, but limited. This limitation was the only thing I missed about brand X, as they had some amazing color designs. Then series 2 was released.
I have to say that I am very pleased with the unique and vibrant colors that have been added with this expansion. I never knew I would be attracted to a pearlescent pink until I saw it! The color names are ridiculous and fun. If Wiz Dice can keep this up into a third expansion I will be a happy customer. For people who must collect the whole set, they offer complete bags with all available colors per series in one place, rather than a random selection each time.

The magnifying glass is probably the most fun tool for my child, and the little amber stone even has a cute fly that got stuck inside. The dinosaurs can either remain flat, or can stand upright with the attachable supports. One thing that's a bit hard is getting the dinos to fold down enough to put them inside the rocks that open and close. The dinosaurs (and fossil puzzle pieces) are felt material, so they should soften and become more flexible with continued use, so that issue will likely improve. The toolbox is handy for storing the little pieces inside. The actual product box is pretty nice too, and could be used for storage as well. I think it’s a great activity toy!

Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage I was disappointed in this microscope, BUT it is for preschoolers. Each part was designed with them in mind. It doesn't magnify much, but it's for the benefit of their eyes. It's also designed so that they don't have to shut one eye to see. It's simple! If you're looking for something more advanced, you'll most definitely want to go another route. This one is more of a toy than a microscope.

It comes with 24 slides, with 3 items on each one. (Plus one blank one.) There's an included book that tells what it is on each of the slides(page 27 and 28). There's no storage for these at all. It would have been nice for a container or bag of some sort to be included to hold all of these. For now, we have the microscope and the slides within a basket, and that makes it easy to pull it off the shelf.

To use the light part of the microscope, you have to put in 2 AAA batteries, which are not included. Flip the switch and a light will come on. Just place a slide under the lens. (It will only go one way.) There's a knob that turns on the front, and this will move the slide back and forth. That's it. There's no way to zoom in and out.

I wouldn't recommend this microscope unless you want it as the most basic introduction to very young children(5ish and under). Even then if they've already been introduced to a microscope, they'll probably be disappointed in this one.
text_fidelity_b: Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage

text_fidelity_a:
Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Civilization: A New Dawn is indeed a new dawn in board gaming for this tried and true franchise. The Sid Meier property has had multiple iterations of previous games, each briging more and more complexity to the table. A New Dawn dials that back a good deal, abstracting many concepts, and doing away with large numbers of pieces and systems in favor of a more streamlined, simple and abstracted system.

And in almost every case, this new system works extremely well. Science and technology is particularly interesting to play with, requiring you to make great sacrfices in power and ability to move up the track in search of new ability. Even the game's winning conditions are easier to understand - the game's goal cards have two halves, and simply by fulfilling one side of each of three cards, you'll earn a victory. These neat and tidy new systems removed huge numbers of pieces from the game, and made the whole thing fit into a nice smaller sized box with a modular board for exploration, a nice touch from previous editions, many of which took place on a fairly boring board that looked like a small island.

The one area where the streamlining process fails, and where that failure comes down quite hard, is in the military systems. There is still a combat mechanic in the game, but because the game took away so many of the unit pieces and simplified down the fighting system, there is very little strategy, and many game-altering battles will be a simple "who rolls higher" contest with no modifiers or rerolls. This takes an otherwise strategic and highly contested game and breaks it all down to luck, ruining a large part of the experience for many.

This fatal flaw in the game is a big reason for my dislike of the game, but the game overall is quite good. It's a shame that this one element is going to make the game so polarizing. It's fun to a certain extent, but it does quite frequently just come down to randomness at the end.
text_fidelity_b: Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a:
My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV I like this game console, but really just think it's something that a few people will enjoy more than most. The design of the console is really good, the look of the main unit is very well done. The wireless controllers are decent enough and feel well made. It's the games though that count. The games are a bit underwhelming. There is a good variety of games, from card games (solitaire, go fish, and a few others of that kind) to puzzle games (sudoku, sliding block puzzle, a pattern block puzzle). There are also many arcade style games. This model of the console does not have any of the old Data East arcade games on it. There is another version that does. The front of the box for that one will have graphics showing the Data East games.

I was sort of expecting the games on this to be the same as what is on most of these sort of consoles (famiclone games), but instead these are a bit more generic than even those. Some of the games are difficult to figure out, it took me about 10-15 minutes or experimenting to figure out how the controllers worked with the sudoku game, and even after I did - the controls were so awkward it made playing the game nearly impossible (and given that this game is timed, I never could achieve a decent time in solving the puzzle). Still, there are many that are worth playing. I think one of the reasons I like game systems like this is the challenge of figuring out what makes the game work.

The main game unit take four double A batteries and the wireless units take triple-A batteries (three each). The console hooks to the TV via a composite video cable (yellow RCA plug) and has one audio input (another RCA plug). I'm using the front inputs on my old VCR which is still connected to my television. I like that the controllers are wireless. You don't really need both, many of the games are for single player. The controllers are marked (P1 & P2), as the P1 controller is the main one and it is used to select the games from the menu.

All-in-all, I am enjoying most of these games, and appreciate the game system for what it is - but I would imagine that many people might not.

This system is made by My Arcade Gaming, and I have one of their handheld Go Gamer Portable games which I purchased last year around Christmas time. I was sort of hoping that this new game console would have the same set of games on it that their handheld model has (which are really good by the way), but that wasn't the case.
text_fidelity_b: My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV

Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone This is an easy-to-learn game with minimal set-up. It’s fast-paced and the rounds and the games go quickly. The circular game board has letters from which to select and a 10-second time. A player draws a card and picks one of two categories to play, such as “Pizza Toppings”. The first player thinks of something that fits that category, such as “Cheese”, and presses the “C” on the board. The next player now needs to think of a pizza topping, but can’t use the letter “C”. Play continues until only one player remains. Then, the round is over and the next player chooses a card.

The game requires 2 “AA” batteries that are not included. There is a storage place on the bottom of the game board for the cards. If the timer wasn’t so loud, it would be a great game for the car. It would be good to bring on a trip to play once you arrived, since it’s compact with self-contained storage for the cards. This is a great game for families because the cards are double-sides with different difficulty levels on each side.

It was harder than it seems to come up with things that fit the category beginning with one of the available letters, within the time-limit. Younger kids may get bored after a few rounds, but great game for passing a short amount of time. It would be nice if it came with more cards, because if it did become a family favorite, it wouldn’t take long to go through the cards. Still, it’s a fun family game.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

FurReal Friends Hop `N Cuddle Tan Bunny The Furreal Friends Hop 'N Cuddle Bunny (Tan color) is a nice toy for a young child. Rabbits are one of the more popular animals with little kids, and a stuffed animal like this that the child can control is a great idea, particular for a young girl like my niece who is completely bunny-crazy, and may be too young to own the real thing.

The bunny has a switch with three settings located on the bottom hidden by a velcro slot. "Try Me," for temporary activity, "Off," and "On." The "on" switch activates the one minute sequence of crawling in a circle approximately 3 feet in diameter (going clockwise), with occasional stops, sitting up, and various noises that I suppose to the right young person could be considered endearing. The sequence lasts long enough for the bunny do do a little more than one circular loop. It worked just fine on our carpet. I haven't tried it on the hardwood.

The "on" sequence will stop after about a minute, but if you gently brush a switch located on the bunny's lower back near the tail, the sequence starts again. My niece quickly figured out the mechanism, and sleeps with the bunny next to her, occasionally pushing the button if she wanted some motion or sounds. It stops after a short while if she does not.

The construction seems reasonable. The faux fur has been sewn over a hard shell animatronic body. There are pink pads on the bottom of the bunny feet. So this bunny is not squishable, and may not give the best hugs. I clicked four stars on the durable, but of course it hasn't been in action long enough to judge this.

However, I have noticed that she prefers her animals to make friends with each other and converse. After quickly learning the geometry of the pattern, she sits another animal where she expects the bunny to be at the end of its circular path, then begins narrating the important commands, statements, and then, when the bunny finally gets to the other stuffed animal, friendly greetings are exchanged between the two stuffed acquaintances. Adorable.
text_fidelity_b: FurReal Friends Hop `N Cuddle Tan Bunny

text_fidelity_a:
Asmodee Hit Z Road This is a very silly game, despite the theme. Not a gory or cartoonish zombie game, it really could be almost anything in place of them: Mad Max-style marauders, for instance. What's nice about that is, if you're anything like me, and you're totally over all types of zombie games, you will still be able to play Hit Z Road.

This game is really a push your luck dice rolling game with auctions. You're trying to survive until the end of the road, and you need to make some meaningful choices along the way that could make your journey much easier, or much more daring. There is some player elimination, but it's not one of those "you can die on the first turn" types of eliminations - our earliest death was about 10 minutes before the end of the game.

I think a lot of people will find the artwork on this game to be fantastic, and I have to admit that it is daring, different, and one of the most unique looking games out there. While I can admire the work that went into it, the art just doesn't appeal to me.

The name, by the way, might be one of the worst in the history of board gaming.
text_fidelity_b: Asmodee Hit Z Road

The construction is average - hard plastic and is a typical Scandinavian blonde, blue-eyed beauty. The mechanisms that transform her from a princess to a cape wearing flying machine work well enough but the two short tubes sticking out from her back sort of creep me out. Your Barbie-lover will have this doll figured out in a mere moment so going into detail as to how it works is really not necessary.

It is a pretty cool idea but I don't think I would care to spend $25.00 (as of this review) on it.

This has a "pen" attached with a string, writing on the surface produces nice, legible lines and the button on the bottom slides from right to left to "erase" what's on the board.  Much faster, neater and cleaner to use!  Granted, the screen has different colors in certain areas of the board meaning that if you write on the far left side you get a nice, black line, but the further right you go with the line, you get other colors.  Not a bad thing, but just be aware it isn't all black on the board.  Still, I like it for my own needs just as it is.

text_fidelity_a:
JURASSIC WORLD GYROSPHERE BLAST Vehicle My 9 year old son has had an obsession with Jurassic Park/Jurassic World for years now. His last Halloween costume was Dr. Alan Grant, if that tells you anything. It's all we hear from his mouth 95% of the time. His mind lives in the world of the movies. It was his pleasure to try out these toys and then tell me his favorite things about them. For this one, I had read some negative reviews before ordering, and I asked him about their complaint. "I don't know why someone would complain about such a good toy, mama", was his response.

He loves that there are claw marks all over the vehicle, like a dinosaur has clawed it. While he was telling me about how it works, he discovered more claw marks and a Jurassic logo at the bottom of the vehicle and became excited. "That's why you should explore your toys. You never know what secrets might be in your toys, " he told me.

The gyrospere part works well most of the time. It occasionally gets stuck from coming out, but while I was watching, it was usually when the vehicle was tilted slightly upwards, causing it to fall back downhill. It requires no batteries, thankfully. There's a button on top that releases the gyrosphere when it's pressed. It doesn't come with people, other than a little cardboard Owen. My son also loves that it has 6 wheels, because "That is amazing!".

So, my son loves this toy!
text_fidelity_b: JURASSIC WORLD GYROSPHERE BLAST Vehicle

Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit I am a Lego fan, but I kept that in mind as I reviewed this, not wanting it to make my review unfair.
So, lets start with the kit. The pieces do not fit together as well as Lego pieces do. That’s not a huge thing, but it’s a little annoying with some of the steps.
I have to say that the instructions are much better than Lego ones –MegaBlox devised a very clear way to show what piece to put, and where to put it. That was nice. However, they lace the style Lego shows – if this were a Lego set, it would be hollow – allowing things to go inside it – this set is solid, no room inside for anything. The feet fall off easily, which gets old fast.

Plus there are many “special” bricks that will limit the owners ability to make other things out of the set. Although, that is moot if you have a sizable MegaBlox collection already.

The finished piece is nice – a little boxy – think Minions meets Minecraft.

My issue is the price though. If you look at Lego sets (aside from brand ones like Disney and some of the collectable ones) the cost is around 10c per brick.
This set works out at almost 30cents per brick. Three times the cost of a comparably sized Lego set.
The quality does not warrant that price. Despite the added value of the Despicable Me brand. If it was rounder, more interactive, or had stronger feet I would be inclines to give it a better score

If the shortcomings don’t bother you, and your life *needs* all things “Despicable Me” then you will enjoy this.
If someone else is paying for it, you will find it a bargain.

Otherwise I would recommend you get your Despicable Me and building set fix from a better product.
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit

text_fidelity_a: Crayola Oil Pastels, Assorted Neon Colors, Gift for Kids & Adults, 12 Count I bought these and used them in my first attempt at oil pastels which I have included in my photo along with samples of each color. The colors really do look neon in the light. There is no black or white. I would have liked more colors so I purchased a bigger set, but I'm glad I have the neons. I purchased the Crayola brand because I read many reviews that recommended this brand as high quality. Since I didn't have any experience I can't say whether they were better than any others but they were certainly easy to use and  I was able to draw something I liked even with just the few colors. I think adding neon to all the other bigger sets is  a great way to produce really polished work. These crayon pastels are really easy to layer and you can also scratch designs into the surface to reveal another color if you so desire. This set provides all three values... cool, warm, and neutral, so you can produce good work without having every color you would like to have or you can just buy more because they don't cost much especially the Crayola brand. I bought the bigger set and also their portfolio set. If you choose to smudge them using your finger you will get a colored finger. You can clean your fingers with baby wipes or soap, and even lotion is helpful at removing stains. Also you could use a blender tool like a paper tortillon. I used my finger. I hope I answered any questions you might have. There are lots of good tutorials on how to use pastels on YouTube also. This is a fun medium for people who don't want to spend a lot of money but like a good time.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Oil Pastels, Assorted Neon Colors, Gift for Kids & Adults, 12 Count

Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Speedtropolis Track Set This is a really fun piece for a Hot Wheels set. I liked it a lot. It has three places where you can connect other tracks and sets, which is cool, because then you can connect other sets or tracks with it. The best part is the part where cars make a one and a half times turn around from the top level to the floor.

There's a car elevator that's supposed to bring cars from the floor to the top level. However, this is really hard to move, and requires so much force that the car will fly off the elevator before you can successfully levitate it to the top. None of the tracks that come with this can be used with other sets, because of the way they fit together. So, if you misplace any pieces, then you really have to throw the whole thing away, or put it in your junk plastic pile. But, those are the only two negative things.

The car elevator has a place you can lift up, and that's really fun for little kids, especially ones that are still learning motor skills. The car that mine came with is really cool, but I think there's a different car in every set. Overall it's a great set.
